content.abstract_summary: Extends conformal prediction theory to non-exchangeable data settings via weighted conformal prediction and permutation-invariance relaxations. Provides rigorous finite-sample coverage bounds when training and test distributions differ or data points exhibit dependency structures, establishing the mathematical basis for conformal inference on clinical data.
key_findings: Standard conformal prediction guarantees 1 - α coverage only under exact exchangeability (i.i.d. data)
Introduces weighted non-conformity scores with provable coverage bounds under arbitrary known covariate shifts and bounded non-exchangeability
Establishes robustness bounds showing coverage degradation is strictly bounded by the total variation distance from exchangeability
Applicable to clinical and longitudinal datasets where distributional shifts occur across treatment cohorts
limitations: Bounds depend on estimating or bounding departure from exchangeability
Prediction set efficiency can widen substantially under severe non-exchangeability

extracted_claims.text: Conformal prediction offers distribution-free, finite-sample predictive inference, but standard guarantees rely heavily on data exchangeability.

gaps_addressed: Fills Pillar 2 (M2.2) theoretical requirement for adapting conformal prediction to non-exchangeable pharmacometric clinical trial data

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Foundational mathematical reference for Pillar 2 M2.2 conformal prediction extension.
